internship.title: Full Stack Web Development Internship
internship.description: A research-driven, engineering-oriented internship that progresses from web platform fundamentals through responsive accessible frontend development, typed JavaScript, React, Node.js/Express APIs, PostgreSQL/Prisma data modeling, authentication, security, testing, performance and release engineering, culminating in one integrated full-stack marketplace project.
internship.level: Intermediate-to-advanced, with foundations included for interns who meet the prerequisites

estimatedDuration.workload: approximately 12–15 focused hours per week; actual pace depends on prior experience and project depth
estimatedDuration.basis: Design estimate derived from the breadth of the researched full-stack scope, module tasks, practical work and final project; not a claim about an external internship duration.

prerequisites: Basic JavaScript familiarity is recommended but the early modules revisit the web platform and language foundations.
Ability to use a terminal and editor.
Basic Git familiarity is helpful but not mandatory.
objectives: Understand the browser-to-database request lifecycle.
Build accessible responsive web interfaces.
Use JavaScript and TypeScript for application logic.
Build typed React clients.
Build Express APIs with validation and error handling.
Model and query PostgreSQL through Prisma.
Implement authentication, authorization and session security.
Test behavior with component and browser-level tests.
Measure performance and prepare deployment plans.
Work with Git, documentation, debugging and review-oriented engineering practices.
Deliver and explain one substantial full-stack project.

competencies.evidence: Request traces, HTTP contracts and data-flow explanations.

competencies.evidence: Semantic HTML, responsive CSS, React components and state.

competencies.evidence: Express middleware, resource routes, validation and error handling.

competencies.name: Data engineering
competencies.evidence: PostgreSQL relationships, Prisma migrations, constraints and indexes.

competencies.name: Security
competencies.evidence: Password/session implementation, authorization matrix, threat model and XSS review.

competencies.name: Testing
competencies.evidence: Behavior-focused component tests and Playwright smoke tests.

competencies.evidence: Measurement plans and query/layout review without fabricated benchmarks.

competencies.name: Engineering workflow
competencies.evidence: Git branches, acceptance criteria, debugging notes, documentation and release review.

competencies.name: System thinking
competencies.evidence: Final project architecture, data flow, deployment and troubleshooting explanation.

researchMethodology.scope: Research covered official web platform guidance, React/TypeScript, Express, Node.js release status, Prisma/PostgreSQL, Git/GitHub collaboration, OWASP security guidance, WCAG, Docker Compose, Testing Library, Playwright and Web Vitals.
researchMethodology.versionSnapshot: The package/runtime choices were checked against current official/package sources during research. React 19.2 is the current React documentation version; Node 24 is an LTS release line; TypeScript 7.0.2, Vite 8.2.2, Express 5.2.1 and Prisma 7.10.0 were selected from current stable package/documentation evidence. Prisma 8 was not used because the current research identified it as a newer major/recommended path with release-candidate status while Prisma 7.10 remains a stable supported path.
sourcePrinciples: Use multiple authoritative sources for broad full-stack topics.
Do not invent URLs, package names, test results or deployment evidence.
Separate educational architecture choices from externally verified facts.

lessons.notes: Pure functions are easier to reason about because their output depends on explicit inputs rather than hidden browser or database state.

quiz.explanation: Types disappear at runtime and do not validate arbitrary input.

lessons.notes: fetch() rejects for request-level failures, not simply because a server returned 404. Application code should inspect the Response and parse error payloads safely.

quiz.question: What should a fetch wrapper inspect?
quiz.explanation: HTTP failure is distinct from a network-level rejection.

tasks.title: Build a safe Express error boundary
objectives: Create HttpError and final error middleware.
tasks.hint:
export class HttpError extends Error{constructor(public status:number,message:string){super(message)}}
export function errorHandler(error:unknown,_req:any,res:any,_next:any){if(error instanceof HttpError)return res.status(error.status).json({error:error.message});console.error(error);return res.status(500).json({error:"Internal server error"})}
tasks.solutionCode: The boundary gives clients safe errors while retaining diagnostics.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The solution directly addresses the task: Build a safe Express error boundary. It is intentionally limited to the stated requirement and does not claim unperformed runtime results.

objectives: Validate strings and positive prices before persistence.

constraints: Reject invalid data before DB access.
tasks.hint:
function requireString(value:unknown,field:string,min=1,max=200){if(typeof value!=="string")throw new Error(`${field} must be a string`);const v=value.trim();if(v.length<min||v.length>max)throw new Error(`${field} length invalid`);return v}
function requirePositiveInt(value:unknown,field:string){const n=Number(value);if(!Number.isInteger(n)||n<=0)throw new Error(`${field} must be positive`);return n}

lessons.title: Password hashing and sessions
lessons.description: Build safer credential and session handling.
lessons.notes: OWASP recommends Argon2id where available and scrypt as an alternative with appropriate parameters. Session identifiers should be random, meaningless and server-managed. The project uses Node scrypt with N=2^17, r=8, p=1 and SHA-256 token storage hashes.

quiz.question: Why store a hash of the session token server-side?
options: To reduce value of a database-only disclosure
quiz.answer: To reduce value of a database-only disclosure
quiz.explanation: The raw token remains with the client; the database stores only a verifier.

project.heading: Build a Full-Stack Local Service Marketplace
project.description: Build a multi-role web application where customers discover provider-created local services, request bookings, track booking status and review completed work. Providers create service listings and manage incoming bookings. The project exercises browser UI, HTTP APIs, authentication, authorization, relational persistence, testing, security, responsive design and operational thinking as one integrated system. It deliberately uses locally created records rather than fabricated marketplace data.
project.problemStatement: Local service discovery often requires a customer to find a service, understand its provider and price, request a suitable time, and then track whether the provider accepted and completed the request. Build a small but coherent marketplace workflow that makes those interactions explicit while enforcing identity, ownership and data-integrity rules on the server.
objectives: Design a full-stack architecture with a React client and Express API.
Persist users, services, bookings, reviews and sessions in PostgreSQL.
Implement authentication with secure password derivation and server-side sessions.
Enforce role and object ownership authorization on the API.
Build a responsive and accessible user interface.
Test important UI and browser behaviors with Vitest/Testing Library and Playwright.
Review security, performance, deployment and operational risks honestly.
functionalRequirements: Customers can register, sign in and sign out.
Providers can register, sign in and publish service listings with title, description, category, city and price.
Visitors can search services by text and city.
Customers can request a future booking for a service.
Providers can confirm and complete their incoming bookings.
Customers or providers can cancel an eligible booking according to the server's authorization rules.
Customers can review a booking only after it is completed and only once.
The application exposes a health endpoint for operational checks.
technicalRequirements: React 19.2.8 with TypeScript for the client.
Vite 8.2.2 for client development and production build.
Node.js 24 LTS as the recommended runtime.
Prisma ORM 7.10.0 with @prisma/adapter-pg and pg for PostgreSQL access.
Cookie-based server sessions with HttpOnly cookies.
Vitest and React Testing Library for component behavior tests.
Docker Compose for local PostgreSQL infrastructure.
uiRequirements: Use semantic headings, landmarks, labels and native controls.
Keep primary flows keyboard accessible and visibly focused.
Support mobile, tablet and desktop layouts without intentional horizontal overflow.
Provide distinct loading, empty, success and error states.
Render user-provided text as text rather than executable HTML.
securityRequirements: Use scrypt with a documented work factor and per-password salt.
Generate high-entropy session tokens and store only a server-side hash.
Use HttpOnly session cookies and secure cookies in production.
Reject unexpected Origin values on state-changing API requests.
Enforce role and resource ownership authorization on the API.
Do not log passwords, session tokens or secrets.
Do not expose server stack traces to clients.
Do not put authentication credentials in localStorage or sessionStorage.
testingRequirements: Run the client component test suite.
Run Playwright after installing its browser binaries.
Exercise authentication, service discovery, booking authorization and review eligibility as additional regression scenarios during the internship.
Record actual command output when validating a deployment; do not invent pass/fail results.

architecture.style: Layered monolithic web application for the internship project
architecture.boundaries: The browser is untrusted. Express is the application trust boundary. PostgreSQL enforces relational integrity. Session meaning is stored server-side.
architecture.dataFlow: User → React UI → /api request → Express middleware → route handler → validation/authorization → Prisma Client → PostgreSQL → JSON response → React UI.
architecture.authFlow: Register/login → password verification → random session token → SHA-256 token hash stored in Session row → HttpOnly cookie sent to browser → later request carries cookie → server hashes cookie token → loads non-expired session/user → authorization checks continue.
architecture.bookingFlow: Customer selects service → client sends serviceId and future scheduledAt → server authenticates customer → validates date → verifies service exists → creates Booking → client reloads booking list.
architecture.errorFlow: Route throws HttpError for expected client conditions or an unexpected error → final Express error middleware logs unexpected failures → client receives a safe JSON error.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Defines the relational marketplace data model and integrity constraints.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The implementation matches the stated architecture and is intentionally self-contained for the internship project.
fileWiseSolution.code:
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client"
  output   = "../src/generated/prisma"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
}

enum UserRole {
  CUSTOMER
  PROVIDER
  ADMIN
}

enum BookingStatus {
  PENDING
  CONFIRMED
  COMPLETED
  CANCELLED
}

model User {
  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  email        String     @unique
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         UserRole   @default(CUSTOMER)
  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt
  services     Service[]  @relation("ProviderServices")
  bookings     Booking[]  @relation("CustomerBookings")
  reviews      Review[]
  sessions     Session[]

  @@index([role])
}

model Service {
  id          String    @id @default(cuid())
  title       String
  description String
  category    String
  city        String
  priceCents  Int
  providerId  String
  provider    User      @relation("ProviderServices", fields: [providerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  bookings    Booking[]
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([category, city])
  @@index([providerId])
}

model Booking {
  id         String        @id @default(cuid())
  customerId String
  serviceId  String
  status     BookingStatus @default(PENDING)
  scheduledAt DateTime
  customer   User          @relation("CustomerBookings", fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  service    Service       @relation(fields: [serviceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  review     Review?
  createdAt  DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime      @updatedAt

  @@index([customerId, status])
  @@index([serviceId, scheduledAt])
}

model Review {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  rating     Int
  comment    String
  bookingId  String   @unique
  authorId   String
  booking    Booking  @relation(fields: [bookingId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  author     User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([authorId])
}

model Session {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  tokenHash String   @unique
  userId    String
  expiresAt DateTime
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([expiresAt])
}

fileWiseSolution.code:
# Local Service Marketplace — Final Project

This project is the final practical assessment for the **Full Stack Web Development Internship**.

## What it builds

A local-services marketplace with:

- customer and provider accounts
- server-side session authentication using an HttpOnly cookie
- provider-created service listings
- service search by text and city
- customer booking requests
- provider booking confirmation/completion
- customer reviews after completion
- PostgreSQL persistence through Prisma ORM
- responsive React UI
- unit/component and end-to-end test examples
- baseline security headers, same-origin checks, validation and safe error responses

The project intentionally does not ship seed records or pretend that external provider/customer data exists. A learner creates real records locally through the UI.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 LTS or newer supported Node release
- npm
- Docker Desktop or another Docker Engine/Compose installation
- a browser

## Setup

### 1. Start PostgreSQL

From the project root:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

### 2. Configure the API

```bash
cd server
copy .env.example .env
npm install
npx prisma generate
npx prisma migrate dev --name init
```

On macOS/Linux, copy the file with:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Keep the development values local. Never commit `.env`.

### 3. Start the API

```bash
npm run dev
```

The API runs on `http://localhost:4000`.

### 4. Start the client

Open another terminal:

```bash
cd client
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the Vite URL printed by the terminal, normally `http://localhost:5173`.

## Testing

Client component test:

```bash
cd client
npm test
```

End-to-end tests:

```bash
npx playwright install
npm run test:e2e
```

Server type/build check:

```bash
cd server
npm run build
```

## Data model

`User` owns services and customer bookings. `Service` belongs to a provider. `Booking` connects a customer to a service and has a controlled status lifecycle. `Review` is one-per-booking and only becomes possible after completion. `Session` stores a SHA-256 hash of a random session token and an expiry time.

## Security notes

- Passwords are derived with Node's `scrypt`; plaintext passwords are never stored.
- Session tokens are random, stored only as hashes in the database, and sent to the browser as HttpOnly cookies.
- Mutating requests reject an unexpected `Origin`.
- JSON body size is capped.
- Security response headers are set centrally.
- Validation is performed on the server, not just in browser forms.
- Errors returned to clients do not expose stack traces.
- No secrets are embedded in client source.
- The UI renders user content as React text rather than injecting HTML.

This is an educational project. Before real deployment, add operational controls appropriate to the threat model, including rate limiting, centralized secret management, database backups, monitoring, dependency update automation, TLS termination, and a production review of cookie/CORS/session policy.

## Architecture

Browser → Vite React client → same-origin `/api` proxy in development → Express API → validation/auth middleware → Prisma Client with PostgreSQL driver adapter → PostgreSQL.

Production can serve the built client from a static host or reverse proxy and run the API/database separately. The exact provider is intentionally not assumed.

## Troubleshooting

- If Prisma cannot connect, confirm Docker is running and `DATABASE_URL` matches the Compose credentials.
- If the browser reports API failures, confirm the API is listening on port 4000 and the Vite dev server is running on port 5173.
- If Prisma generated imports are missing, run `npx prisma generate` from `server`.
- If Playwright browsers are missing, run `npx playwright install`.

project.howItWorks: The client starts by attempting `/api/auth/me` and then loads services. Registration/login creates a server-side session and returns only the safe user identity. Provider users can create services; customers can create future bookings. The booking route checks the authenticated role and service existence before writing. Providers can move bookings through confirmation/completion; completed customer bookings become reviewable. React renders returned strings as text. The API applies security headers, same-origin checks, validation and ownership authorization before database mutations.

testing.component: The included Vitest/Testing Library test mocks the API module and verifies the marketplace heading through an accessible role query.
testing.e2e: The included Playwright test loads the app and checks the main heading and sign-in navigation; the config includes desktop and iPhone 13 projects.
testing.server: The server build uses strict TypeScript compilation. A database integration suite is intentionally not claimed as executed because it requires a running PostgreSQL instance and installed dependencies.
additionalCases: Registration rejects short passwords and malformed fields.
Provider cannot create service as CUSTOMER.
Customer cannot create provider-only service listings.
Provider cannot delete another provider's service.
Only completed bookings can be reviewed.
A booking cannot receive a second review.

implemented: scrypt password derivation with per-password random salt and N=2^17, r=8, p=1.
Random 32-byte session tokens; only SHA-256 token hashes are persisted.
HttpOnly, SameSite cookie; Secure enabled in production.
Server-side validation of strings, integers and dates.
Security response headers including CSP baseline, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and frame denial.
No password/token logging in application code.
No user-controlled HTML injection API in the client.
Booking status transitions are constrained on the server, and services with booking history are protected from deletion.
limitations: No rate limiter is included; add one before public deployment.
Password reset, MFA, email verification and account recovery are outside the educational scope.
Production secret management, TLS termination, backups and monitoring must be implemented at deployment time.
The project uses SameSite=Lax plus Origin checking; deployment architecture should be reviewed if the frontend/API become cross-site.
A full dependency vulnerability scan was not executed in this environment.

guidance: Measure Core Web Vitals and request timing before optimizing.
Keep service list responses bounded to 50 records in the current educational implementation.
Avoid rendering unnecessary state and keep components focused.
Configure production logging and connection pools according to the actual workload.
performance.noFabricatedBenchmarks: No benchmark or Core Web Vitals result is claimed. The internship teaches how to measure them.

deployment.architecture: A production deployment should place the React static build behind a TLS-enabled web server/CDN, run the Express API in a managed or containerized service, and use a managed PostgreSQL instance or hardened database host. Exact providers are intentionally not assumed.
steps: Build the client with `npm run build`.
Build the server with `npm run build`.
Configure production environment variables and secret storage.
Apply reviewed database migrations to a staging database first.
Configure TLS and the final frontend/API origin.
Run health checks and smoke tests.
deployment.truthfulness: No production deployment was performed or claimed.

checks: Run `npx prisma generate` after dependency installation.
Confirm API is listening on port 4000.
Confirm Vite is using its /api proxy.
Inspect DevTools Network and server logs.
Confirm the schema output points to `src/generated/prisma`.
